new_statements.second_reader_evidence: records the sealang.net download. I re-rendered p. 2 at 110 dpi and read it: header 'Pampaŋo Phonology', consonant/vowel chart, a 'morphophonemics' column (aa > aya), then a bottom block 'Stress:' with ʔápiʔ 'lime' / ʔapíʔ 'fire' / bábaʔ 'chin' / babáʔ 'underneath' in the left column and ápu 'grandparent (mother)' / apú 'grandchild' on the right, and a 'Length:' block with anák 'child' / a:nak 'children', babái 'woman' / ba:bai 'women', talá Ds / tá:la Dp. Every form, gloss and label in the compiler quotation is on the sheet exactly as transcribed. I also read pp. 3-15 (pronouns and deictics pp. 3-6, negatives p. 7, verb affixes and focus paradigms pp. 8-12, proto-morphology word list p. 13…
new_statements.relation_note: The catalog holds a Kapampangan record with an empty rule field and no existing statements. Zorc's notes supply the first concrete data for it: contrastive (phonemic) stress, penult vs ultima minimal pairs, and an independent vowel-length contrast. Nothing to contradict. Note for the compilers: Gonzalez 1981 (Pacific Linguistics C-48, already held by the project in the same folder from the compilation of 9/16, not in this task's work list) says the same in prose on pp. 15-16: 'the distinctive feature accented must be posited as one of the features of the Pampangan sound system. Thus, there are minimal pairs.. which differ in their symbolisation only by the position of the accent', and adds…
new_statements.rule_in_words: The sheet gives no prose rule; it lists minimal pairs in which the only difference is stress on the penult versus the final syllable (ʔápiʔ 'lime' vs ʔapíʔ 'fire'; bábaʔ 'chin' vs babáʔ 'underneath'; ápu 'grandparent' vs apú 'grandchild'), i.e. word stress is lexically contrastive and not positionally predictable. A separate 'Length:' block shows vowel length as an independent contrast used morphologically (anák 'child' vs a:nak 'children'; talá dual-singular vs tá:la dual-plural), and elsewhere in the notes length marks progressive aspect (su:sulat, ma:tudtud, ma:g-ʔaral, pp. 8, 9, 12).
new_statements.exceptions: None stated. Stress is marked on individual lexical items throughout the notes and on the Proto-Philippine worksheet (p. 17: nánu, nínu, kanínu, kapilán, bákit, pilán, alé?), consistent with item-by-item lexical stress; verb paradigms on pp. 8-9 show stress shifting with affixation (magdaláʔ / megdaláʔ / ma:gdala; sáliʔ / sinalíʔ / sa:salíʔ; sópan / sinópan / sosópan) but no rule is given.
new_statements.identity_note: The handwritten notes name no dialect or locality. The Proto-Philippine worksheet in the same bundle (p. 17) is headed 'Kapampaŋan' with the consultant's name 'Leonardo Pineda' written at the top right; the language is elsewhere called 'Pampaŋo' / 'Pampango' in the notes. Same language as the catalog's Kapampangan (pamp1243).
